participants: Marcus Trent (Meridian, account owner); Janet Feld (VP supply chain, Kellerman Industrial)
body:
[CALL TRANSCRIPT — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042) | QBR 2025-01-21 | ref CRM-9001]
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: Janet, thanks for taking this. I know the last two weeks have been rough — I want to own it.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: Rough is generous, Marcus. The Chicago storm buried a whole batch of our freight. One of our loads was on the truck that jackknifed.
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: I know, and it's documented on our side. No injuries, and we recovered the load, but I'm not going to pretend the delay didn't hurt you.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: It did. My question is whether you can actually handle our peak volume, because right now I'm not sure.
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: Fair. Two things: we're issuing an SLA credit for January per your contract, and I'll bring you a written recovery plan. I want to keep earning this.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: I'll wait for the credit and the plan. But consider this a warning shot.

[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: I saw the credit, thank you. Recovering is fine. Not-there-yet is the part I'm watching.
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: Understood. No weather excuse this quarter — the gap's on us to close.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: As long as the trend is up, we're constructive. Keep me posted between QBRs.

participants: Marcus Trent (Meridian, account owner); Janet Feld (VP supply chain, Kellerman Industrial)
body:
[CALL TRANSCRIPT — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042) | QBR 2025-07-16 | ref CRM-9021]
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: Janet, I'm not going to spin this. On-time slipped again this quarter and your ticket volume is up.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: Right, and there was no storm this time. We logged three late LTL loads in the last month alone. My team is escalating internally.
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: I'm moving your account to a watch status on our side so it gets more attention. I owe you a concrete improvement plan by the next review.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: I need more than a plan on a slide, Marcus. I need the loads to show up.
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: Understood. Weekly, not quarterly, from here.

participants: Marcus Trent (Meridian, account owner); Janet Feld (VP supply chain, Kellerman Industrial)
body:
[CALL TRANSCRIPT — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042) | QBR 2025-10-14 | ref CRM-9022]
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: Thanks for making time. I'll be straight: the trend is still down and I know you're looking at other carriers.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: We are. I'd be doing my job badly if we weren't. A year ago you were healthy for us; today you're a risk.
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: I hear that, and I'm treating it as at-risk. I've written a formal save plan — dedicated Chicago capacity for your freight through peak, a weekly on-time scorecard, and an exec sponsor.
[Janet Feld — Kellerman]: The dedicated capacity is the part that matters. If peak goes the way January did, we're done.
[Marcus Trent — Meridian]: Then peak is where we prove it. You'll have the scorecard every Monday.
